related_questions.question: Is it safe to travel to Nigeria right now?

text_blocks.snippet: It's not recommended to travel to Nigeria right now due to safety concerns. Many countries advise against all but essential travel due to a high risk of crime, terrorism, and civil unrest. Some specific areas have even higher risk levels and travel is advised against.
snippet_highlighted_words: It's not recommended to travel to Nigeria right now due to safety concerns

list.title: High Risk:
list.snippet: Several countries advise against non-essential travel to Nigeria due to the unpredictable security situation and significant risk of terrorism, crime, inter-communal clashes, armed attacks, and kidnappings.

list.title: Specific Threats:
list.snippet: Terrorist groups like Boko Haram and ISWAP are active, particularly in the northeast. Kidnapping, including for ransom, is a serious concern, and can occur anywhere in the country.

list.title: Regional Variations:
list.snippet: Some regions, like the northeast, are more dangerous than others. Certain areas have specific travel advisories recommending against travel, while others advise against travel to areas accessible only by boat.

list.title: Safety Precautions:
list.snippet: Even in areas where travel is permitted, it's crucial to exercise a high degree of caution. Travelers should be aware of their surroundings, avoid large crowds and demonstrations, and take precautions against petty crime.

list.title: Government Advisories:
list.snippet: Refer to your own government's travel advisories for the most up-to-date information on specific regions and safety recommendations.

related_questions.question: Is the COVID pandemic still going on?

text_blocks.snippet: While the World Health Organization (WHO) declared an end to the COVID-19 Public Health Emergency of International Concern (PHEIC) on May 5, 2023, COVID-19 continues to circulate. The pandemic's official end is not clearly defined, and whether it's still considered a pandemic depends on the definition used. Currently, COVID-19 vaccines continue to offer protection against severe disease and death according to the WHO.
